messages:
support_tina: FYI acme-inc (acct: acme-42) reporting repeated 503s on hosted inference since ~09:05 UTC. Customer says timeouts + 'upstream error' in the response body.
customer_ops_ron: They pasted a snippet from their side: 
```
{"error":"upstream error: worker exited unexpectedly (code 137)"}
```
and they also see request ids: r_8a7c3f...

sre_jordan: On it — pulling logs for the pod serving that model now. looks like a restart spike.

sre_jordan: kubectl logs -n hosted svc-infer-xyz --since=10m | tail -n 50
```
[2026-03-17T09:04:21Z] runner: allocating CUDA context on GPU 0
[2026-03-17T09:04:25Z] kv_cache: prefetch 128MB
[2026-03-17T09:05:02Z] runtime: Caught signal SIGSEGV (fault addr=0x7f8f1c2)
[2026-03-17T09:05:02Z] runtime: aborting worker (exit 139)
[2026-03-17T09:05:02Z] infer-api: returning 503 upstream error
```

infra_derek: dmesg from node ip-10-0-1-23 shows repeated GPU resets and nvme complaints: 
```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 1234.567895] NVRM: GPU 0000:65:00.0: GPU reset detected.
[ 1234.567900] kernel: watchdog: BUG: soft lockup in worker_thread
```

ml_maria: The model runner logs show kv cache memory allocation spikes just before the segfault — looks like a memory surge then SIGSEGV inside the attention kernel. Could be a combination of driver/runtime mismatch + higher batch concurrency.

sre_jordan: Immediate mitigation: cordon + drain ip-10-0-1-23, move affected pods to healthy pool, and enable runtime fallback for acme-inc to the smaller quantized model variant. Executing now.

deploy-bot: fallback route engaged for customer acme-42 -> model: redwood/llama2-q4f16-small v1 (forced compat) :information_source:

support_tina: I told the customer we enabled a temporary fallback and asked them to retry. suggested client-side retry/backoff and setting concurrency=1 for now.

customer_ops_ron: They retried 3x and reported success on the fallback. still want a permanent fix, said this impacts production traffic.

infra_derek: Preliminary root cause hypothesis: driver 535.12 on kernel 6.1.12 is triggering GPU resets under high-concurrency KV prefetch patterns. We saw similar on canary last week but lower frequency. Next steps: pin driver to 534.86 on this fleet, repro with stress harness, and roll out fix. Opening infra ticket IR-2026-113.

ml_maria: Repro steps I'm using: stress binary + load generator hitting /v1/generate with:
```
for i in {1..200}; do
  curl -s -X POST https://hosted.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"model":"redwood/llama2-large","input":"test","max_tokens":512,"batch_size":8}' &
done
wait
```
We see OOM-ish allocations then segfault after ~90s at concurrency 150. Lowering batch_size to 1 prevents the crash.

sre_jordan: Action items: (1) infra to pin driver and schedule rolling update for affected pool (infra_derek). (2) ML/Runtime to add defensive checks around KV prefetch and fail gracefully (ml_maria). (3) Support to keep customer updated and confirm SLA impact (support_tina). I've set incident severity P2.

support_tina: Customer accepted fallback and asked for ETA. told them we expect a driver pin + rolling patch within 24-36h, will escalate if that slips. :thumbsup:

infra_derek: Kicking off driver pin now on the affected nodes. will report progress in IR-2026-113.

sre_jordan: Monitoring cluster metrics — restart rate dropped to normal after drain & fallback. keeping page open for next 12h.

support_tina: Closing loop with customer, logging workaround steps, will follow up after infra patch. thanks all :heart:
thread_summary: customer acme-inc experienced 503s due to upstream worker crashes (SIGSEGV/GPU resets). temporary fallback to smaller quantized model applied; infra to pin GPU driver and repro; ml/runtime to add defensive checks.
